summary.title: Disagreement over discipline of our son
summary.what_happened: Our son Aram is 9. He had not done his maths homework and it was 8pm. My husband Daniel raised his voice, said Aram was lazy, and took away his tablet for two weeks. I told Daniel in front of Aram that he was overreacting. Then I took Aram to his room and let him keep the tablet for that night.
summary.my_feelings: I was unhappy with how Daniel handled it, and I could not say more in front of Aram.
summary.my_needs: I need us to decide on rules together instead of Daniel deciding alone.
summary.desired_outcome: I want Daniel to be calmer with Aram, and for us to agree on rules together.

consult.text:
It sounds like you felt stuck last night. You saw something that bothered you, and you could not say it the way you wanted in front of Aram. That is a hard spot for a parent.

Daniel may see this differently. He may have been tired and worried about the homework, and he may feel he is the one who has to hold the line on rules. If he thinks you often step in, he may feel alone in parenting and unsupported.

One thing that may have made this harder is the way it played out. Telling Daniel he was overreacting in front of Aram, and then letting Aram keep the tablet, may have left Daniel feeling overruled. It could also have shown Aram that the two of you disagree. Your concern about the tone and the two-week punishment can still be fair.

We do not know how Daniel felt afterwards, or whether this has happened before.

Some next steps:
- Talk to Daniel when you are both calm, not in front of Aram.
- Start with what you saw and what you need, such as agreeing on rules together.
- Decide together what happens with the tablet, so Aram hears one plan.
So you're saying it's my fault for defending my son?

I can hear that this feels unfair. You were trying to protect Aram, and that matters.

I am not saying defending him was wrong. What I said was narrower. Disagreeing with Daniel in front of Aram, and then changing the outcome, may have left Daniel feeling overruled. That is one piece of what happened. Your worry about how he spoke to Aram is still a real concern.

What you can do now is more useful than who did what last night. You could choose a calm time to talk to Daniel, away from Aram. You could say that you want to back each other up in front of Aram and sort out disagreements in private. You could also suggest agreeing on a few clear rules for homework and screens together.

Would it help to think about how you might start that conversation?

share_draft: Hi Daniel. I want to talk about what happened with Aram's homework last night. I wasn't comfortable with how it went, and I could have waited to tell you in private. Instead I said you were overreacting in front of him, then let him keep the tablet. I know that was hard for you. What I need is for us to agree on rules for homework and screens together, so Aram gets one clear message. I would also like us to find a calmer way to handle moments like that. I'd like to hear how it looked from your side. Could we find a time to talk when Aram is not around?
harsh_draft: You were a bully to Aram last night. You call him lazy and then wonder why he's scared of you. Grow up.

rewrite.rewrite: I thought you were too harsh with Aram last night. I don't think calling him lazy was okay. I'd like you to speak to him more calmly.

perspective_summary: Leila is worried about how her husband spoke to their 9-year-old son after he skipped his maths homework, including the word lazy and a two-week loss of his tablet. She felt she could not speak up in the moment, and she later told Daniel he was overreacting in front of Aram. She wants Daniel to be calmer and wants the two of them to set rules together instead of one parent deciding alone. She expects Daniel may feel she is too soft on Aram.
